name: Clio Manage
description: Clio Manage is cloud legal practice-management software for organizing clients, matters, documents, calendars, tasks, time, billing, payments, communications, and firm operations.
agentUseSummary: Connect one US-region Clio Manage user through Relay-owned confidential OAuth. Relay requests only the application's read-only Users permission and exposes one approval-gated authority check that returns enabled status, fixed region, and API version while discarding identity and all legal-practice data.

scopes: Users (read-only, configured on the OAuth application)

capabilities.label: Verify connection authority
capabilities.description: Verify that the US-region OAuth grant resolves to an enabled Clio Manage user while returning no user identity or legal-practice data.

approvalRequired.label: Verify Clio Manage connection authority
approvalRequired.description: Call the fixed who-am-I endpoint with only id and enabled fields, use the ID only to validate authority, discard it, and return enabled status, US region, and API version.

blocked.label: Access identity, firm, or client data
blocked.description: User IDs and identity fields, firm details, contacts, clients, matters, relationships, custom fields, notes, and all associated legal-practice data are blocked.

blocked.label: Access documents, communications, or calendars
blocked.description: Documents, folders, emails, messages, communications, calendar entries, attendees, tasks, activities, time entries, and expenses are blocked.

blocked.label: Access billing, payments, or financial data
blocked.description: Bills, balances, bank and trust accounts, payments, accounting records, rates, invoices, transactions, and financial reports are blocked.

blocked.label: Write, subscribe, or administer Clio Manage
blocked.description: Creates, updates, deletes, custom actions, webhooks, exports, users, roles, permissions, OAuth applications, and administration are blocked.

blocked.label: Use raw APIs, another region, or bulk access
blocked.description: Arbitrary endpoints, methods, fields, associations, filters, pagination, other Clio regions, browser sessions, scraping, raw responses, bulk operations, and exports are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: The identity-free authority check requires approval; all identity, legal-practice records, content, financial data, writes, webhooks, administration, arbitrary APIs, and other regions remain blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: The same authority check runs directly; US-region binding, read-only Users permission, field minimization, redaction, auditing, response bounds, and provider rate limits remain mandatory.

runtimeSupport.description: Railway mounts one field-minimized authority check and injects OAuth tokens server-side.
Railway mounts one field-minimized authority check and injects OAuth tokens server-side.

providerSetup.blocker: A US-region Clio Manage developer account and public OAuth application, accepted Developer Terms, exact Railway callback, confidential client credentials, only the read-only Users permission, application review and directory approval as applicable, customer consent, refresh/deauthorization validation, security and privacy review, and live acceptance are required.
providerSetup.nextAction: Use the separate provider-console task to apply for the US developer account, create the OAuth app with only read-only Users permission and the exact Railway callback, accept Clio's developer and data requirements, store the client credentials on Railway, and validate authorization, token refresh, identity redaction, 50-per-minute rate handling, deauthorization, disconnect, and post-disconnect denial.

evidence.supports: Clio Manage confidential OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow, exact redirect URI, 10-minute authorization code, 30-day bearer access token, non-expiring refresh token, deauthorization endpoint and callback, and regional token isolation.
Developer applications choose fixed read-only or read/write access permissions; user roles further restrict access, missing permissions return 403, and associated data can be redacted.
Official v4 endpoints, US/CA/EU/AU regions, field selection, who-am-I resource, version header, typed errors, and the much broader legal-practice surface intentionally excluded from V1.
API v4 is rate-limited per access token, defaults to 50 requests per minute during peak hours, returns rate-limit headers and Retry-After on 429, and may change limits.

Clio requires minimum necessary data, applicable consent and authority, encrypted transmission and storage, secret protection, deletion after deauthorization or when no longer required, and use only through documented APIs.
Clio's app guidance requires security, privacy, data-residency, deletion, incident-response, and public-policy readiness for approval.

securityNotes: Relay's US-only V1 configures only read-only Users permission; Clio Manage permissions are fixed on the developer application rather than dynamically requested during authorization.

The sole request is GET https://app.clio.com/api/v4/users/who_am_i?fields=id,enabled with X-API-VERSION 4.0.13. The ID is validated transiently and discarded; name, email, roles, firm identity, and legal-practice data are never returned or persisted.
Requests reject redirects, time out after 20 seconds, cap responses at 1 MB, do not paginate or retry automatically, and preserve 401, 403, 429, and provider-unavailable outcomes.

Contacts, matters, clients, documents, folders, communications, calendar entries, tasks, activities, notes, custom fields, bills, payments, trust and bank accounts, webhooks, custom actions, writes, administration, arbitrary APIs, other regions, bulk access, and exports are unavailable.

Access and refresh tokens remain encrypted server-side; disconnect uses Clio's documented deauthorization endpoint and deletes Relay's grant. Provider-console setup and live acceptance remain external blockers.
